library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("AjavonHartmann_2025_apixaban"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("AjavonHartmann_2025_apixaban"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.3689> (open access, PMC12272319)
* Supplement: Data S1 of the article (estimation methods, pediatric
  demographics, dataset composition, exposure summaries by age group, and the
  model-development schematic)

Ajavon-Hartmann 2025 added the sparse PK data of the phase II SAXOPHONE trial
(children aged 28 days to <18 years with congenital or acquired heart disease,
CAHD, needing chronic anticoagulation for thromboembolism prevention) to the
pooled adult and pediatric apixaban population PK model. It then re-tested the
patient-type covariates and used the model to check the trial's fixed-dose
weight-tiered regimen against adult exposure. The companion paper (Jarugula
2025, `Jarugula_2025_apixaban` in this package) is the same model fitted
before the SAXOPHONE data were added. A zero-intercept linear mixed-effects
regression relates anti-factor Xa activity (AXA) to apixaban concentration.

Compared with the Jarugula 2025 fit, backward elimination here kept the
ALL/LL patient-type effect on ka, dropped it from Vc/F, and added a
CAHD effect on CL/F (Figure S1 of the supplement).

# Population

The final dataset held 6098 apixaban concentrations from 602 patients in 12
studies: 198 adults from eight adult studies, 56 pediatric patients at risk of
venous or arterial thromboembolism from two phase I studies (CV185079,
CV185118), 224 PREVAPIX-ALL patients with acute lymphoblastic leukemia or
lymphoblastic lymphoma on asparaginase (CV185155), and 124 SAXOPHONE patients
with CAHD (CV185362, 447 concentrations; Table S2). Table S1 describes the 404
pediatric patients: age 0.044 to 18 years (median 6.73), baseline weight 3 to
133 kg (median 22.6), 47.3% female, 78.5% White, 7.43% Asian and 6.44% Black.
The SAXOPHONE patients were 0.378 to 18 years (median 7.5) and 6.1 to 133 kg
(median 23.6); none was younger than 4 months. Adult demographics are not
reported. The PK/PD analysis used 390 AXA values from 123 PREVAPIX-ALL and
SAXOPHONE patients, measured with a drug-calibrated assay in ng/mL.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("AjavonHartmann_2025_apixaban")()$population`.

# Source trace

Each `ini()` entry carries an in-file comment naming its source. The table
collects them. The functional forms come from the parameter-covariate
equations under Table 1.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` (adult ka) | log(0.525) 1/h | Table 1, theta1 |
| `lcl` (CL/F, 67.4 kg, mature) | log(4.7) L/h | Table 1, theta2 |
| `lvc` (Vc/F, 67.4 kg) | log(32.5) L | Table 1, theta3 |
| `lq` (Q/F, 25 years) | log(1.43) L/h | Table 1, theta4 |
| `lvp` (Vp/F) | log(20.8) L | Table 1, theta5 |
| `lgamma` (F1 dose shape) | log(0.89) | Table 1, theta6 |
| `logitifdepot50` (logit max F1 reduction) | -0.457 | Table 1, theta7 |
| `e_wt_vc` | 0.882 | Table 1, theta8 |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.68 | Table 1, theta9 |
| `e_age_q` | 0.751 | Table 1, theta10 |
| `e_ped9m_ka` | 1.23 | Table 1, theta11 |
| `lhill` (ontogeny shape) | log(0.83), fixed | Table 1, theta12 |
| `lpna50` (ontogeny AGE50) | log(0.244) years, fixed | Table 1, theta13 |
| `e_form_capsule_fdepot` | 1.1, fixed | Table 1, theta14 |
| `fbirth_cl` | 0.05, fixed | Table 1, theta15 |
| `e_dis_all_ka` | -0.988 | Table 1, theta16 |
| `e_dis_heart_congenital_acquired_cl` | -0.185 | Table 1, theta17 |
| `etalka` | 0.399 | Table 1, ZKA |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc`, covariance | 0.149, 0.0719, 0.0838 | Table 1, ZCL, ZVC, ZVC:ZCL |
| `etalvp`, `etalq`, covariance | 1.39, 0.989, 1.07 | Table 1, ZVP, ZQ, ZQ:ZVP |
| `expSd` | 0.328 | Table 1, sigma 1,1 = 0.108 (SD 0.328), additive on log concentration |
| `slope_antiFXa` | 0.916 | Table 3, slope |
| `etaslope_antiFXa` | 0.0528^2 | Table 3, random-effect standard deviation 0.0528 |
| `addSd_antiFXa` | 12.8 ng/mL | Table 3, residual 12.8 |
| ka equation | `theta1 * (1 + PED9M * theta11) * exp(theta16 if PTYPE = ALL)` | Table 1 equations |
| CL/F equation incl. ontogeny | `theta2 * (WT/67.4)^theta9 * MF * exp(theta17 if PTYPE = CAHD)` | Table 1 equations and MF footnote |
| Vc/F, Q/F, Vp/F equations | see model file | Table 1 equations |
| F1 equation | 1 for dose <= 2.5 mg, else `1 - expit(theta7) * ((DOSE - 2.5)/47.5)^theta6`; times 1.1 for sprinkle capsule | Table 1 equations |
| `Cc = 1000 * central / vc` | ng/mL | dose in mg, volume in L |
| `antiFXa = (slope + eta) * Cc` | ng/mL | Results and Discussion (PK/PD analysis); Table 3 |
| Residual `Cc ~ lnorm(expSd)` | n/a | Results; Supplementary Methods (additive error on log scale) |

# Typical-value checks

The Results quote derived typical values that pin the covariate structure:
ka of 0.525, 1.17 and 0.436 1/h for adults, other children aged 9 months to
<18 years, and children with ALL/LL (17% and 62.8% lower for ALL/LL), and
CL/F of 3.91 L/h for a 67.4-kg CAHD patient against 4.7 L/h for the reference
(16.9% lower). Table 1's footnote gives the IIV correlations 0.809 and 0.912.
These follow from the parameters without any randomness, so they are checked
tightly. The paper's 4.7 and 3.91 L/h are for a fully matured patient; the
CL/F column of the table below includes the maturation fraction (0.98 at 25
years, 0.96 at 10 years), which the check divides out.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("AjavonHartmann_2025_apixaban")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# zeroRe() removes the random effects on purpose; rxode2 warns on every
# multi-subject solve without omega, so muffle that one warning only.
solve_typical <- function(...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}

typ_cov <- tibble::tibble(
  id = 1:4,
  group = c("Adult", "Pediatric other, 9 mo to <18 y", "Pediatric ALL/LL", "Pediatric CAHD"),
  WT = 67.4,
  AGE = c(25, 10, 10, 10),
  DIS_ALL = c(0, 0, 1, 0),
  DIS_HEART_CONGENITAL_ACQUIRED = c(0, 0, 0, 1),
  DOSE_APIXABAN_MG = 2.5,
  FORM_CAPSULE = 0
)
typ_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  typ_cov |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 2.5, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_),
  typ_cov |> dplyr::mutate(time = 1, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

typ <- solve_typical(mod_typ, typ_ev, keep = "group", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::select(group, ka, vc, cl, fmat)

typ |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Group" = group, "ka (1/h)" = ka, "Vc/F (L)" = vc, "CL/F (L/h)" = cl,
    "Maturation fraction" = fmat
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Typical values for a 67.4-kg patient.")

ka_adult <- typ$ka[1]
ka_other <- typ$ka[2]
ka_all <- typ$ka[3]
# The paper's 4.7 vs 3.91 L/h comparison is for a fully matured patient; at
# 10 years the maturation fraction is 0.995, so divide it out.
cl_ref <- typ$cl[2] / typ$fmat[2]
cl_cahd <- typ$cl[4] / typ$fmat[4]

omega <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)$omega
r_cl_vc <- omega["etalcl", "etalvc"] / sqrt(omega["etalcl", "etalcl"] * omega["etalvc", "etalvc"])
r_vp_q <- omega["etalvp", "etalq"] / sqrt(omega["etalvp", "etalvp"] * omega["etalq", "etalq"])

stopifnot(
  abs(ka_adult - 0.525) < 5e-4,
  abs(ka_other - 1.17) < 5e-3,
  abs(ka_all - 0.436) < 5e-4,
  abs(100 * (1 - ka_all / ka_adult) - 17) < 0.5,
  abs(100 * (1 - ka_all / ka_other) - 62.8) < 0.1,
  abs(cl_ref - 4.7) < 1e-6,
  abs(cl_cahd - 3.91) < 5e-3,
  abs(100 * (1 - cl_cahd / cl_ref) - 16.9) < 0.05,
  abs(r_cl_vc - 0.809) < 0.005,
  abs(r_vp_q - 0.912) < 0.005
)
```

# Table 2 internal consistency: dose, bioavailability and clearance

Table 2 reports, per weight tier, the geometric means of the SAXOPHONE
patients' individual CL/F and steady-state AUC(TAU). The paper's AUC equation
is dose x F1 / (CL/F). Evaluated at the tier geometric-mean CL/F with the
dose of each tier and this model's F1, it reproduces the Table 2 AUC(TAU)
column. That pins the twice-daily doses the trial used (1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4 and
5 mg, the regimen proposed in the Results) and the F1 reduction above 2.5 mg,
which only this regimen's 3-, 4- and 5-mg tiers reach. The geometric mean of
a ratio is not the ratio of the geometric means, so the agreement is close but
not exact.

```{r table2-consistency}
t2 <- tibble::tibble(
  tier = c("6 to <9 kg", "9 to <12 kg", "12 to <18 kg", "18 to <25 kg", "25 to <35 kg", ">=35 kg"),
  id = 1:6,
  dose = c(1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5),
  cl_t2 = c(0.682, 0.812, 1.25, 1.64, 2.12, 2.99),
  auc_t2 = c(1460, 1840, 1610, 1760, 1840, 1630)
)
# Solve once per tier only to read the model's F1 at that dose.
f_ev <- t2 |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_,
    WT = 20, AGE = 8, DIS_ALL = 0, DIS_HEART_CONGENITAL_ACQUIRED = 1,
    DOSE_APIXABAN_MG = dose, FORM_CAPSULE = 0
  ) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    t2 |> dplyr::transmute(
      id, time = 1, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L,
      WT = 20, AGE = 8, DIS_ALL = 0, DIS_HEART_CONGENITAL_ACQUIRED = 1,
      DOSE_APIXABAN_MG = dose, FORM_CAPSULE = 0
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
f_tab <- solve_typical(mod_typ, f_ev, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::select(id, frel)

t2_chk <- dplyr::inner_join(t2, f_tab, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    auc_calc = 1000 * dose * frel / cl_t2,
    pct_diff = 100 * (auc_calc / auc_t2 - 1)
  )
t2_chk |>
  dplyr::select(tier, dose, frel, cl_t2, auc_calc, auc_t2, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Weight tier" = tier, "Dose (mg BID)" = dose, "F1" = frel,
    "Table 2 CL/F (L/h)" = cl_t2, "Dose x F1 / CL/F" = auc_calc,
    "Table 2 AUC(TAU)" = auc_t2, "% difference" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 1, 3, 3, 0, 0, 1), caption = "Steady-state AUC(TAU) (ng.h/mL) implied by the Table 2 geometric-mean CL/F.")

# A wrong dose for a tier, or an F1 reduction applied with the wrong sign or
# anchor, moves the affected tier by 20% or more.
stopifnot(all(abs(t2_chk$pct_diff) < 5))
```

# Virtual cohort

The paper simulated about 1000 virtual patients per weight tier (9 tiers),
assigning age, sex and weight as in its companion analyses. The cohorts below
keep 200 patients per tier: for each tier, age is drawn uniformly over the
ages at which the CDC 2000 sex-averaged median weight falls inside the tier
(28 days to <18 years), and weight is the CDC median for that age with 12%
lognormal scatter; a weight that falls outside the tier is redrawn uniformly
within it. All virtual patients have CAHD (`DIS_HEART_CONGENITAL_ACQUIRED = 1`)
and take the tablet or oral solution (`FORM_CAPSULE = 0`).

```{r cohort}
# CDC 2000 50th-percentile weight-for-age, sexes averaged. Reference data for
# building the virtual cohort only, not a model parameter.
cdc_age_yr <- c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24) / 12
cdc_wt_kg <- c(3.4, 4.4, 5.5, 6.3, 7.0, 7.9, 9.0, 9.9, 11.3, 12.5)
cdc_age_yr <- c(cdc_age_yr, 3:18)
cdc_wt_kg <- c(
  cdc_wt_kg, 14.3, 16.3, 18.3, 20.7, 23.2, 26.0, 29.2, 32.7,
  36.7, 41.3, 46.0, 50.6, 54.6, 58.0, 60.6, 62.6
)
cdc_weight_for_age <- function(age_yr) {
  stats::approx(cdc_age_yr, cdc_wt_kg, xout = age_yr, rule = 2)$y
}
cdc_age_for_weight <- function(wt_kg) {
  stats::approx(cdc_wt_kg, cdc_age_yr, xout = wt_kg, rule = 2)$y
}

n_per_tier <- 200L

# One cohort per weight tier; ages restricted to [age_min, age_max).
make_tier <- function(tier, wt_lo, wt_hi, dose, age_min, age_max, id_offset) {
  a_lo <- max(age_min, cdc_age_for_weight(wt_lo))
  a_hi <- min(age_max, cdc_age_for_weight(min(wt_hi, 70)))
  if (a_hi <= a_lo + 1 / 12) a_hi <- a_lo + 1 / 12
  age <- stats::runif(n_per_tier, a_lo, a_hi)
  wt <- cdc_weight_for_age(age) * exp(stats::rnorm(n_per_tier, 0, 0.12))
  # Where the CDC median lies outside the tier (the lightest tiers), clamping
  # would pile patients on one edge; redraw those uniformly inside the tier.
  out <- wt < wt_lo | wt >= wt_hi
  wt[out] <- stats::runif(sum(out), wt_lo, wt_hi)
  tibble::tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n_per_tier),
    tier = tier,
    WT = wt,
    AGE = age,
    DIS_ALL = 0,
    DIS_HEART_CONGENITAL_ACQUIRED = 1,
    FORM_CAPSULE = 0,
    DOSE_APIXABAN_MG = dose
  )
}

# Proposed regimen for ages 28 days to <18 years (Results, PPK model
# simulations); the six tiers from 6 kg are the SAXOPHONE regimen.
tiers <- tibble::tribble(
  ~tier,                  ~wt_lo, ~wt_hi, ~dose,
  "3 to <4 kg, 0.2 mg",      3.0,    4.0,   0.2,
  "4 to <5 kg, 0.3 mg",      4.0,    5.0,   0.3,
  "5 to <6 kg, 0.5 mg",      5.0,    6.0,   0.5,
  "6 to <9 kg, 1 mg",        6.0,    9.0,   1.0,
  "9 to <12 kg, 1.5 mg",     9.0,   12.0,   1.5,
  "12 to <18 kg, 2 mg",     12.0,   18.0,   2.0,
  "18 to <25 kg, 3 mg",     18.0,   25.0,   3.0,
  "25 to <35 kg, 4 mg",     25.0,   35.0,   4.0,
  ">=35 kg, 5 mg",          35.0,  133.0,   5.0
)

set.seed(20250623)
cohort <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(tiers)), function(i) {
  r <- tiers[i, ]
  make_tier(r$tier, r$wt_lo, r$wt_hi, r$dose,
    age_min = 28 / 365.25, age_max = 18, id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_tier
  )
}))
cohort$tier <- factor(cohort$tier, levels = tiers$tier)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(cohort$id))

cohort |>
  dplyr::group_by(tier) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    `median age (y)` = median(AGE),
    `median WT (kg)` = median(WT),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Virtual CAHD cohort (ages 28 days to <18 years).")
```

# Simulation

Twice-daily dosing is simulated directly at steady state (`ss = 1`, `ii = 12`)
with observations every 0.25 h over one dosing interval.

```{r simulate}
tau <- 12
obs_grid <- seq(0, tau, by = 0.25)

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  cohort |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      time = 0, amt = DOSE_APIXABAN_MG, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot",
      dvid = NA_integer_, ss = 1L, ii = tau
    ),
  cohort |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_grid) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L, ss = 0L, ii = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250623)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events,
  keep = c("tier", "DOSE_APIXABAN_MG"),
  maxsteps = 500000L,
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
# A solver failure would drop subjects silently through the PKNCA filter below.
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$Cc), dplyr::n_distinct(sim$id) == nrow(cohort))
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 3: steady-state AUC(TAU) by weight tier

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, antiFXa, tier)

dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, tier)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = tau,
  auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, tmax = TRUE
)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | tier + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | tier + id)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::select(id, tier, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

# Steady-state AUC(TAU) equals F1 * dose / CL for the same drawn parameters;
# the only difference is trapezoidal error on the 0.25-h grid.
cl_by_id <- sim |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, auc_closed = 1000 * DOSE_APIXABAN_MG * frel * fform / cl)
auc_chk <- dplyr::inner_join(nca_wide, cl_by_id, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auclast / auc_closed - 1))
stopifnot(
  abs(median(auc_chk$pct_diff)) < 1,
  quantile(abs(auc_chk$pct_diff), 0.9) < 3
)
```

The Methods describe the Figure 3 simulation as virtual pediatric patients
with CAHD. Simulated that way (`DIS_HEART_CONGENITAL_ACQUIRED = 1`), the tier
medians come out about 20% above the published Figure 3 medians in every tier
from 6 kg upward, and they agree instead with the Table 2 AUC(TAU) of the real
SAXOPHONE patients. A 20% shift in every tier is exactly the CAHD effect on
CL/F, exp(0.185) = 1.20; no difference in the age or weight mix of a cohort can
produce it in the narrow middle tiers, where maturation is complete and weight
is pinned by the tier. The published Figure 3 medians are reproduced when the
same virtual patients are simulated with the reference patient type
(`DIS_HEART_CONGENITAL_ACQUIRED = 0`), so the figure appears to have been
generated without the CAHD clearance effect. Both scenarios are shown below;
the Figure 3 gate uses the reference-type scenario and the Table 2 gate the
CAHD scenario.

```{r figure-3-reference-type}
# Same virtual patients with the reference patient type. Steady-state AUC(TAU)
# is F1 x dose / CL (the paper's AUC equation), so one observation row per
# patient is enough to read the individual parameters.
events_ref <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  cohort |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = DOSE_APIXABAN_MG, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_),
  cohort |> dplyr::mutate(time = 1, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(DIS_HEART_CONGENITAL_ACQUIRED = 0) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250625)
sim_ref <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events_ref, keep = c("tier", "DOSE_APIXABAN_MG"), returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::mutate(auc_ss = 1000 * DOSE_APIXABAN_MG * frel * fform / cl)
stopifnot(dplyr::n_distinct(sim_ref$id) == nrow(cohort), !anyNA(sim_ref$auc_ss))

fig3_sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  nca_wide |> dplyr::transmute(tier, auc = auclast, scenario = "CAHD (indicator = 1)"),
  sim_ref |> dplyr::transmute(tier, auc = auc_ss, scenario = "Reference patient type (indicator = 0)")
)
```

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4.8}
# Replicates Figure 3 of Ajavon-Hartmann 2025 (pediatric tiers): steady-state
# AUC(TAU) against the adult VTE-treatment reference (median 1240, 90% CI
# 675-2300 ng.h/mL).
fig3_published <- tibble::tibble(
  tier = factor(tiers$tier, levels = tiers$tier),
  published = c(937, 1090, 1290, 1440, 1390, 1340, 1480, 1520, 1280)
)

q5_95 <- function(y) {
  data.frame(ymin = quantile(y, 0.05), ymax = quantile(y, 0.95))
}
ggplot(fig3_sim, aes(tier, auc, fill = scenario)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = 675, ymax = 2300, alpha = 0.15, fill = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1240, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, coef = 0, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = q5_95, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  geom_point(
    data = fig3_published, aes(tier, published), inherit.aes = FALSE,
    shape = 4, size = 3, colour = "blue"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey85", "white")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 5000)) +
  labs(
    x = "Weight tier and twice-daily dose",
    y = "Steady-state AUC(TAU) (ng.h/mL)",
    fill = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 3 of Ajavon-Hartmann 2025. Boxes: 25th-75th percentiles;",
      "whiskers: 5th-95th. Blue x: published tier medians."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1), legend.position = "top")
```

```{r fig3-gate}
auc_med <- fig3_sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(tier, scenario) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim = median(auc), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = scenario, values_from = sim) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(fig3_published, by = "tier") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pct_cahd = 100 * (`CAHD (indicator = 1)` / published - 1),
    pct_ref = 100 * (`Reference patient type (indicator = 0)` / published - 1)
  )
auc_med |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Weight tier" = tier, "Figure 3 median" = published,
    "% difference, CAHD" = pct_cahd, "% difference, reference type" = pct_ref
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Steady-state AUC(TAU) medians (ng.h/mL) by simulated patient type.")

# A wrong clearance, weight exponent, maturation function, F1 or unit shifts
# every tier by tens of percent; the tier-to-tier spread reflects only how
# closely the CDC-based cohort reproduces the paper's age and weight sampling.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(auc_med$pct_ref)) < 10,
  all(abs(auc_med$pct_ref) < 25),
  # The CAHD scenario sits one CAHD effect, about 20%, above the figure.
  abs(median(auc_med$pct_cahd) - 100 * (exp(0.185) - 1)) < 10
)
```

## Comparison against published values (Table 2)

Table 2 reports geometric means of the individual (Bayesian) estimates for the
124 SAXOPHONE patients by weight tier. `ncaComparisonTable()` compares the
simulated medians of the six SAXOPHONE tiers with them.

```{r nca_compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~tier,                  ~auclast, ~cmax, ~cmin, ~tmax,
  "6 to <9 kg, 1 mg",         1460,   185,  57.9,  2.14,
  "9 to <12 kg, 1.5 mg",      1840,   218,  82.7,  2.46,
  "12 to <18 kg, 2 mg",       1610,   222,  64.3,  1.72,
  "18 to <25 kg, 3 mg",       1760,   244,  67.4,  1.65,
  "25 to <35 kg, 4 mg",       1840,   249,  73.1,  1.69,
  ">=35 kg, 5 mg",            1630,   203,  72.7,  1.89
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "tier",
  units = c(auclast = "ng.h/mL", cmax = "ng/mL", cmin = "ng/mL", tmax = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Simulated (median, virtual CAHD cohort) vs published (Table 2 geometric",
    "means of SAXOPHONE individual estimates). * differs from reference by >20%."
  )
)
```

The two sides differ in kind: Table 2 summarises the empirical Bayes estimates
of the actual SAXOPHONE patients, who had few samples each (shrinkage on the
etas of ka, Q/F and Vp/F was 36 to 38%), while the simulation draws a full
virtual cohort with the population variances. Only six patients sit in the
6 to <9 kg tier and two in the 9 to <12 kg tier, so those reference values are
themselves imprecise. Cmax, Cmin and Tmax are therefore descriptive. AUC(TAU)
is checked at the centre only: across the six tiers the median difference
between the simulated CAHD medians and the Table 2 geometric means must be
small.

```{r table2-auc-gate}
t2_auc <- nca_wide |>
  dplyr::group_by(tier) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim = median(auclast), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(published |> dplyr::select(tier, auclast), by = "tier") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim / auclast - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(t2_auc) == 6, abs(median(t2_auc$pct_diff)) < 10)
```

## Figure 4: anti-factor Xa activity

The PK/PD model is a zero-intercept line with a normally distributed slope
(mean 0.916, SD 0.0528) and an additive residual SD of 12.8 ng/mL. The
simulated AXA below is computed from the model-predicted concentration, so
the scatter about the line combines the slope variability and the residual
error. Figure 4 plots observed AXA against observed apixaban concentration.

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 5.5, fig.height = 4.5}
ini_df <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)$iniDf
stopifnot(
  abs(ini_df$est[ini_df$name == "slope_antiFXa"] - 0.916) < 1e-9,
  abs(sqrt(ini_df$est[ini_df$name == "etaslope_antiFXa"]) - 0.0528) < 1e-6
)

# Add the residual error to the PK/PD output: rxSolve returns predictions
# without residual error for each endpoint.
set.seed(20250624)
axa_obs <- sim_nca |>
  dplyr::slice_sample(n = 3000) |>
  dplyr::mutate(antiFXa_obs = antiFXa + stats::rnorm(dplyr::n(), 0, 12.8))

ggplot(axa_obs, aes(Cc, antiFXa_obs)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.6) +
  geom_abline(slope = 0.916, intercept = 0) +
  labs(
    x = "Apixaban concentration (ng/mL)", y = "Anti-FXa activity (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Model relationship underlying Figure 4 of Ajavon-Hartmann 2025 (median line)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()

# The ratio antiFXa / Cc is each patient's slope, so its distribution must
# reproduce the Table 3 mean and SD.
slopes <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(Cc > 1) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(slope = antiFXa / Cc)
stopifnot(
  abs(mean(slopes$slope) - 0.916) < 0.01,
  abs(stats::sd(slopes$slope) - 0.0528) < 0.01
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Figure 3 patient type.** The Methods describe the Figure 3 virtual
  patients as children with CAHD, but the published tier medians are
  reproduced only when the CAHD effect on CL/F is switched off, and sit about
  20% (exp(0.185)) below the CAHD simulation and below the Table 2 AUC(TAU) of
  the real SAXOPHONE patients. The model keeps the published CAHD effect; the
  vignette shows both simulated patient types and gates Figure 3 against the
  reference-type scenario.
- **Patient-type covariates.** The paper's single patient-type variable
  (`PTYPE`) is carried as two binary indicators. `DIS_ALL` = 1 for the
  PREVAPIX-ALL patients (acute lymphoblastic leukemia or lymphoblastic
  lymphoma on asparaginase, pooled as in the paper's footnote) and
  `DIS_HEART_CONGENITAL_ACQUIRED` = 1 for the SAXOPHONE patients; both 0
  selects healthy adults and the pediatric phase I patients at risk of
  thromboembolism. The ALL/LL indicator acts on ka only, the CAHD indicator
  on CL/F only. The authors suggest the lower CL/F in CAHD reflects the
  Fontan circulation of most SAXOPHONE patients; the indicator is also
  confounded with study.
- **PED9M** is derived inside the model from `AGE` (1 for 9 months <= age <18
  years), matching the Table 1 footnote definition.
- **Formulation.** The sprinkle-capsule relative bioavailability (1.1, fixed) is
  carried by the general capsule indicator `FORM_CAPSULE` (1 = sprinkle
  capsule); the reference is tablet or oral solution. The paper does not say
  which SAXOPHONE patients took the sprinkle capsule, so all virtual patients
  here take the reference formulation.
- **Dose-dependent bioavailability** reads the dose from the
  `DOSE_APIXABAN_MG` column, which must equal the event-table `amt` on the dose
  records. The SAXOPHONE doses per weight tier are not tabulated; the doses
  used are the regimen proposed in the Results, which the Table 2 consistency
  check above confirms.
- **PK/PD random effect.** Table 3 reports a random-effect standard deviation
  of 0.0528 for the linear mixed-effects regression with 'IIV in the slope
  parameter' (Discussion). It is encoded as a normally distributed, additive
  random effect on the slope (`slope_antiFXa + etaslope_antiFXa`), the usual
  form of a linear mixed-effects random slope. The PK/PD model was fitted to
  observed apixaban concentrations; here it is driven by the model-predicted
  concentration `Cc`.
- **PK/PD dataset size.** The Methods give 541 concentrations from 253
  patients for the PK/PD dataset; the Results give 390 AXA values from 123
  patients after excluding values below the 35 ng/mL quantification limit and
  values without a time-matched concentration. The model metadata quotes the
  Results.
- **Virtual cohort.** Weight-for-age uses the CDC 2000 sex-averaged median with
  12% lognormal scatter instead of sampling the full sex-specific distribution,
  and ages are drawn within each weight tier. This mainly affects the age and
  weight mix inside a tier, and so the tier medians, by a few percent. The
  three lightest tiers (3 to <6 kg) are below the weight of any SAXOPHONE
  patient and are model extrapolations, as in the paper.
- **Cohort size.** 200 virtual patients per tier, against the paper's about
  1000 per tier.
- **Adult reference.** The adult VTE-treatment median of 1240 ng.h/mL (90% CI
  675-2300) is taken from the paper's text; adults are not simulated here.
- No erratum or correction notice for this article was found as of 2026-11-10.
